record.context_brief: Whether GP-UCB can attain tight regret
record.original_question: In the same kernelized bandit setting with an unknown function f in an RKHS and maximal information gain gamma_N, can the standard GP-UCB algorithm, or a simple variation of it that still relies on a standard online confidence bound, achieve regret O~(sqrt(N gamma_N)) on compact domains instead of the currently derived O~(gamma_N sqrt(N)) bound?

evidence.quote: Following standard UCB-based bandit algorithm techniques, it can be shown that the GP-UCB algorithm (namely, repeatedly choosing x to maximize the current upper confidence bound) attains R(N) = O~(rho_N(delta) sqrt(N gamma_N)), with probability at least 1 - delta. Substituting rho_N(delta) from Theorem 2, we have R(N) = O~(gamma_N sqrt(N)).

In view of this discussion, the improvement from O~(gamma_N sqrt(N)) to O~(sqrt(N gamma_N)) has now been obtained using several different algorithms, but it remains to determine whether GP-UCB (or a simple variation thereof) can achieve it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact domain, and let $k: \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a positive definite kernel with associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) $\mathcal{H}_k$. Consider an unknown target function $f \in \mathcal{H}_k$ with $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_k} \le B$ for some known constant $B>0$. At each round $t = 1, 2, \dots, N$, a learner selects $x_t \in \mathcal{X}$ and observes $y_t = f(x_t) + \varepsilon_t$, where $\varepsilon_t$ are independent $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian noise variables. The cumulative regret is
$$R(N) = \sum_{t=1}^{N} \bigl(f(x^*) - f(x_t)\bigr), \qquad x^* \in \arg\max_{x \in \mathcal{X}} f(x).$$
For a Gaussian process surrogate model with prior covariance $k$ and noise variance $\sigma^2$, define the maximal information gain after $N$ steps as
$$\gamma_N = \max_{A \subset \mathcal{X},\, |A|=N} \tfrac{1}{2}\log\det\bigl(I + \sigma^{-2} K_A\bigr),$$
where $K_A = (k(x,x'))_{x,x'\in A}$. The GP-UCB algorithm selects
$$x_t \in \arg\max_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \bigl(\mu_{t-1}(x) + \rho_t \, \sigma_{t-1}(x)\bigr),$$
where $\mu_{t-1}, \sigma_{t-1}$ are the posterior mean and standard deviation given $\{(x_s, y_s)\}_{s<t}$, and $\rho_t$ is a confidence parameter derived from a standard online RKHS confidence bound.

Question: Can the GP-UCB algorithm, or any simple variant of it that still relies on a standard online confidence bound, be shown to achieve cumulative regret $R(N) = \widetilde{O}\bigl(\sqrt{N \gamma_N}\bigr)$ on compact domains, rather than the previously established bound $R(N) = \widetilde{O}\bigl(\gamma_N \sqrt{N}\bigr)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (Whitehouse, Wu, Ramdas, "On the Sublinear Regret of GP-UCB", NeurIPS 2023 / arXiv:2307.07539) tightens the analysis of GP-UCB by regularizing the kernel ridge estimator in proportion to kernel smoothness and applying concentration in separable Hilbert spaces. This yields nearly optimal sublinear regret for GP-UCB on common kernels (notably Matérn), partially resolving the open question. The exact $\widetilde O(\sqrt{N\gamma_N})$ rate is not fully attained for all kernel classes, so the problem is considered partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On the Sublinear Regret of GP-UCB
status_evidence.snippet: We show that GP-UCB enjoys nearly optimal regret, yielding sublinear regret rates for the Matérn kernel, improving over the state-of-the-art analyses and partially resolving a COLT open problem posed by Vakili et al.
status_evidence.claim: Tighter analysis of GP-UCB partially resolves the open problem of attaining the improved regret rate.

status_evidence.title: On the Sublinear Regret of GP-UCB (NeurIPS 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Existing analyses yielded suboptimal regret rates... we provide a tighter analysis of the GP-UCB algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: GP-UCB itself can be analyzed to give improved sublinear regret on standard kernels.
